positive_control_a_link_reversal.description: The a->link reversal mechanism must be preserved or explained under full-DOM correction
positive_control_a_link_reversal.expected: Full-DOM correction changes or reverses the a->link-driven ordering
positive_control_a_link_reversal.observed: DEF-FULL-MAP ordering changes from cart>product_listing>detail to cart>detail>product_listing. Product_listing and detail swap: product_listing has more <a> tags (393-397) but they are undercounted in truncation; under full DOM, detail pages have proportionally similar <a> counts but lower absolute counts, causing the swap.

positive_control_ordering_reversal.description: If truncation drives the ordering, full-DOM correction must change the ordering
positive_control_ordering_reversal.expected: At least 1 definition shows ordering change
positive_control_ordering_reversal.observed: All 3 definitions show ordering changes between truncated and full-DOM

null_control_random_baseline.description: Random 20-element samples from locatable pool should show lower mean absolute bias than first-20 truncation for DEF-FULL-MAP
null_control_random_baseline.expected: Random sample bias < truncation bias for all tasks
null_control_random_baseline.observed: All 7 tasks show random bias < truncation bias (mean trunc=0.2921, mean random=0.2888)

degeneracy_control.description: Tasks with locatable_elements < 20 are excluded from random sample analysis
degeneracy_control.observed: Minimum locatable_elements is 21 (cart_1); all tasks included

observations: DEF-FULL-MAP truncated ordering (cart>product_listing>detail) changes to (cart>detail>product_listing) under full-DOM correction. Product_listing loses its #2 position because its <a> tag count (393-397) is high but almost none appear in the first-20 sample (only 2 per task), while detail pages also have high <a> counts (324-325) that are similarly undercounted.

The relative bias is extreme: 98.2-98.6% for DEF-FULL-MAP across all 7 tasks. The first-20 sample captures only 5-8 interactive elements out of an estimated 324-458 in the full DOM, meaning the truncation discards >95% of interactive elements.

DEF-FORM-ONLY ordering also changes: truncated (product_listing>cart>detail) becomes (product_listing>detail>cart). Cart and detail swap because the truncation captures most of cart's form-related elements (3/3 button+combobox) but only a fraction of detail's (2/6). However, the full-DOM correction for DEF-FORM-ONLY is much smaller in magnitude (64-69% bias) because form-related elements are fewer in the DOM overall.

The a->link mapping is the primary driver of the bias magnitude: DEF-FULL-MAP (which includes a->link) shows 98%+ bias, while DEF-FORM-ONLY (which excludes a->link) shows 64-69% bias for listing/detail and only 1.6% for cart.

Cart page is the least affected by truncation for DEF-FORM-ONLY (1.6% bias) because it has very few form-related elements (2 buttons, 1 combobox) and the truncated sample captures all of them. For DEF-FULL-MAP, cart still shows 98% bias because the 318 <a> tags dominate.

Random sample baseline confirms the bias is due to document-order selection, not small sample size: for DEF-FULL-MAP and ISOLATED-A-LINK, random 20-element draws from the locatable pool produce lower absolute bias than the first-20 truncation for all 7 tasks. For DEF-FORM-ONLY, random samples show higher bias because the truncated sample happens to capture the form-related elements well (they appear early in document order in the header/nav area).

The positive control (a->link reversal) is confirmed: DEF-FULL-MAP ordering includes cart at #1 in both truncated and full-DOM, but product_listing and detail swap positions. The full-DOM reveals that detail pages actually have higher interactive density than product_listing pages once all <a> tags are counted.
All 7 tasks have locatable_elements > 20 (range: 21-82), so no degenerate cases. The cart_1 task has only 21 locatable elements, meaning the first-20 sample captures 95% of the pool.
validity_notes: Full-DOM role counts for <a>, <button>, <form>, <input> use raw DOM tag counts (dom_stats), which include ALL tags in the DOM, not just locatable ones. The locatable pool is a subset of elements_with_bbox which is a subset of total_dom_elements. The full-DOM estimate thus represents an UPPER BOUND on the true locatable count for these roles.

For non-tag-mapped roles (combobox, div, label, span), full-DOM estimates are derived by scaling truncated-sample counts by (locatable_elements / sample_size). This assumes the truncated sample is representative of the pool for these roles, which may not hold if these roles are concentrated in specific DOM regions.

The random sample baseline constructs an approximate locatable pool using DOM proportions scaled to locatable_elements count. This is an approximation because: (1) not all DOM tags are locatable, (2) the role distribution in the locatable pool may differ from the DOM, (3) the pool composition is inferred, not observed.
Single site (Magento shopping), single run. Cross-site generalization is unsupported. All 7 tasks are from the same site with similar DOM structure.

Small N per page type: 3 product_listing, 3 detail, 1 cart. Within-type variance cannot be estimated for cart. Cross-type comparisons are underpowered but the effect sizes are large enough (98% bias) that this is unlikely to change the conclusion.

The full-DOM estimate uses dom_stats.linksCount (393 for listing_clothing) which counts ALL <a> tags. Some of these may be non-interactive (e.g., anchor links, footer links, hidden links). The true locatable <a> count is likely lower, but the truncation bias direction and magnitude remain valid.

DEF-FORM-ONLY C3 (random baseline) fails because the truncated sample captures the form-related elements well (they appear early in document order in the header/nav). Random sampling from the pool includes elements that are NOT form-related, increasing the denominator without adding to the numerator. This is expected behavior, not a measurement error.
unresolved: The true locatable <a> tag count is unknown — dom_stats gives total DOM <a> count (393-397 for listings), but the locatable subset is likely smaller. The bias magnitude may be somewhat overestimated if many <a> tags are non-locatable.
Cross-site replication is needed to determine whether the a->link truncation bias generalizes to sites with different DOM structures (e.g., sites where product links appear early in document order).

The DEF-FORM-ONLY C3 failure suggests that truncation bias depends on which roles are being measured. For form-heavy definitions, the truncation may be unbiased or even favorable (if form elements appear early in DOM). This needs investigation with more diverse page types.

The ordering change under full-DOM correction (product_listing vs detail swap) should be validated with full-DOM enumeration (locatableSample cap removal in runtime lane) rather than tag-count estimation.
Menuitem and tab counts are 0 in this sample, so their contribution to bias cannot be tested. A sample with non-zero menuitem/tab counts is needed.
The single cart page (n=1) limits within-type variance estimation. More distinct cart pages would strengthen the cart vs listing/detail comparison.
